chief_complaint: Uncontrolled stage 2 hypertension and metabolic risk factors with recent gout diagnosis
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 58-year-old Asian Hispanic female with a long-standing history of obesity, hyperlipidemia, prediabetes, anemia, and chronic sinusitis. Blood pressure recorded at 133/94 mmHg meets stage 2 hypertension criteria and is being treated only with low‑dose amlodipine 2.5 mg, which is likely insufficient. Lipid management consists of low‑dose simvastatin 10 mg, and recent lipid values are unavailable. Prediabetes (A1c 5.9%) persists without pharmacologic therapy. In October 2023 she was diagnosed with gout, but no urate‑lowering or anti‑inflammatory medication is documented. Key laboratory data (BMI, eGFR, uric acid, iron studies, full lipid panel) are missing, limiting assessment of cardiovascular and renal risk. Socially, she is a refugee since 1997, employed full‑time, and has higher education, which may influence health‑care access and adherence.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include multiple episodes of viral sinusitis (most recent 2023-09-08), recurrent gingivitis (last resolved 2022-12-14), documented stress (resolved 2022-11-30), part‑time employment (resolved 2022-11-30), and several medication‑review reminders. No chronic diseases other than those listed as active have been resolved.
